title.en: How I Taught My Grandmother to Read (Sudha Murty)

text.en: Is there an age after which we stop learning? In this true account, a twelve-year-old girl becomes the teacher of her sixty-two-year-old grandmother, and the lesson goes both ways.

The narrator recalls her childhood village in north Karnataka, where the morning papers and weekly magazines reached late, carried by the bus that also brought the post.
In those days the Kannada writer Triveni was very popular. Her novel Kashi Yatre appeared as a serial in the weekly Karmaveera.
It told of an old lady who longed to go to Kashi, but who finally gave her savings to help an orphan girl's wedding, saying the girl's happiness mattered more.
The narrator's grandmother, Krishtakka, whom she called Avva, had never been to school and could not read, so every Wednesday the narrator read the next episode aloud to her.
When the narrator stayed a week at a wedding, the magazine came and Avva could not understand a word of it. She was in tears, feeling dependent and helpless although the family was well-off.
That night Avva said she had lost her mother young, never went to school and wanted to be independent. She would learn the Kannada alphabet from the next day and read a novel by Saraswati Puja.
The narrator first laughed at the idea, but Avva answered that for a good cause nothing stops a determined person and that for learning there is no age bar.
On Dassara Avva touched her young teacher's feet and gave her a gift, saying she respected a teacher whatever the age or gender. The narrator gave her Kashi Yatre, and Avva read the title at once, passing with flying colours.

problem.en: What does Avva's statement 'I want to be independent' tell us about her?

text.en: She could not read the magazine and felt helpless.
She did not want to depend on others even though she was well-off.
So the line shows her determination and self-reliance.

prompt.en: Retell the story in five sentences and say what it teaches.

requiredIdeas.en: She decided to learn at sixty-two

points.en: The narrator, a child, taught her grandmother to read.
Avva's determination shows there is no age bar to learning.
A teacher deserves respect regardless of age.
